name: Ethiopian Citizenship by Descent (Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003) -- gender-neutral since 2003

qualifying_event.description: Any person is an Ethiopian national by descent where either or both parents is/are Ethiopian. The 2003 law is described by secondary legal commentary as having removed a gender-discriminatory rule present in Ethiopia's prior 1930 nationality law -- both mothers and fathers can transmit citizenship equally under the current statute. An abandoned infant found in Ethiopia is presumed (rebuttably) to have an Ethiopian parent, though Ethiopian law has no separate statelessness-prevention protection for children born in Ethiopia to non-Ethiopian parents who would otherwise be stateless.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; either parent's proof of Ethiopian nationality.

requirements.blocker_text: Either or both parents was/were an Ethiopian national at the time of birth.

sources.title: African Child Policy Forum (hosting the full text) -- Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003: 'Any person shall be an Ethiopian national by descent where both or either of his/her parent is Ethiopian'; abandoned-infant presumption of Ethiopian parentage

Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative (NGO tracking African nationality law) -- analysis characterizing the 2003 law as removing gender discrimination present in Ethiopia's earlier 1930 nationality law, and flagging a gap: no statelessness-prevention protection for children born in Ethiopia to non-Ethiopian parents who would otherwise be stateless

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ethiopia). STATUS: DRAFT -- the core descent rule is tier-2 sourced from the statute text itself; the tier-4 NGO source is cited only for its historical/comparative characterization (that the 2003 law reformed a gendered 1930-law gap) and its identification of a genuine statutory gap on statelessness prevention -- neither is used for a hard requirement. POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING, WORTH FLAGGING GIVEN THIS DATASET'S RECURRING PATTERN OF GENDERED CITIZENSHIP ASYMMETRIES: Ethiopia's CURRENT law (since 2003) is gender-neutral on descent -- both mothers and fathers can transmit citizenship equally, in explicit contrast to the patrilineal-only patterns found in Qatar's and Bahrain's descent laws built elsewhere in this dataset. The claim that the PRE-2003 law had a gender gap is plausible but only secondary-sourced (tier-4) -- not independently verified against the 1930 statute's own text in this pass, so treated as historical context rather than a hard dataset fact. A genuine, sourced statelessness-prevention gap exists in current law for foundlings/children of unknown-nationality parents who are not covered by the abandoned-infant presumption -- disclosed as a real gap in Ethiopian law itself, not a research limitation.
